questions.question:

We watched the workmen to repair the tiles of the kitchen.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Let's look at the following points-**

__
 
• In the given context Watched will be followed by **'gerund'** instead of **'Infinitive'**
 
• we use the gerund form of a verb when the action isn’t completed.
 
• Since the sentence denotes incompletion of the task hence, therefore gerund will be used in the given context
 
• Hence,** to repair** **the tiles** will be replaced with** replacing the tiles**
 
• **The correct sentence- ***We watched the workmen **repairing **the tiles of the kitchen.*

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **To **is a **preposition **that is used to indicate 

 
 
• Motion in the direction of (a particular location).

 
 
• ​**Example**: *Walking down to the shops*.
 
 
 
• Approaching or reaching (a particular condition).
 
 
• ​**Example**: *His expression changed from happy to joy. *
 
 
 
• **To **is also used with **bare infinitives** i.e (present tense verb used without to) when there is a need to indicate the** purpose or intention of action**** **or to make a comment or judgement. 
 
 
• **Example**: *I am going **to play**. She came **to collect **her paycheque. . *

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

The tree was uprooted by the storm last evening, __isn't it?__
questions.solution:
The **correct answer** is **Option 1** i.e. **"wasn't it".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sentence uses** the past simple passive voice indicated by "**was uprooted".**
 
• The **correct tag question** for a statement in the past simple passive voice should match in both tense and polarity.
 
• The original tag **"isn't it?**" mismatches the main clause's tense (past) as it is in the present tense.
 
• To correct the error, the tag should use** "was"** to match the past tense of the main clause, and "not" to invert the polarity, resulting in "wasn't it".

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- 'Wasn't it'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Was it: **This option matches the tense but does not correctly invert the polarity for a tag question; tag questions should be in the opposite form (affirmative if the statement is negative and negative if the statement is affirmative).
 
• **Didn't it:** This option does not correctly match the form of the verb in the main clause. "Didn't" suggests a simple past active voice, whereas the sentence is in the past passive voice.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to ﬁll in the blank.**

If only we ______ a light! It is depressing to wait in the dark.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Had**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Reading the above sentence we find that: 

__
 
• It talks about possessing something. And also that the tense of the subject is in the past. 
 
• In the given sentence at present light is not there and it is dark. 
 
• Thus it is conveying the meaning that: Light should have been there, but at present, it is not there. 
 
• Here, we should first understand that '**have**' has another meaning apart from the one where it is a helping verb.
 
• '**Have**' also means to be in **possession of something**. 
 
• The construction of the sentence in the** past tense** as the action of possessing the light source is something which is in the past.

Thus, the past tense form of the verb '**have**' ie. '**had**' is the perfect fit here. 

Therefore the correct sentence will be: 'If only we **had **a light! It is depressing to wait in the dark.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

The people mentioned in the sentence are already waiting in the dark in the present time. 

'If only' refers to an imaginary/hypothetical situation and is always followed by a verb in the past tense. Hence, the past tense form of have- 'had' must be used here.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to ﬁll in the blank.

Milk is ______ than any other food.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:** more nourishing**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **Comparative degree** of an adjective denotes a higher degree of the quality than the positive and is used when **two things** are **compared**.

 
 
• For example: This book is **more interesting** than the other one.
 
 
 
• **​**Similarly, in this question, 'milk' is compared with other food using 'than'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Milk is **more nourishing**__ than any other food.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• An **adjective** is a part of speech that describes the noun and pronoun. In most of the cases the adjective comes before the noun it is describing.
 
• The **Positive Degree** of an adjective is the adjective in its simple form. It is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.
 
• The **Comparative degree** of an adjective denotes a higher degree of the quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.
 
• The **Superlative degree** indicates the highest degree of the quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Across his morning walk on a beach in Mamallapuram, Prime Minister Modi was seen picking up plastic litter, bottles, and other items.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Across means from one side to the other of (a place, area, etc.).
 
• For eg; I ran across the road.
 
• The use of 'across' is incorrect in the context of the sentence given above. 
 
• 'During' means throughout the course of something. 
 
• Instead of 'across', 'during' should be used.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

INFINITE
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.**

**Infinite** means limitless or endless in space, extent, or size; impossible to measure or calculate.

For eg; I have infinite mercy of God on me.

Boundless means unlimited or immense.

For eg; She devotes boundless energy on her hobbies.

Vast means of very great extent or quantity; immense.

For eg; There was a vast area of barren land.

**Limited **means restricted in size, amount, or extent; few, small, or short.

For eg; There are a limited number of options with me.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.**

LAMENT
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

**Lament** means a passionate expression of grief or sorrow.

For eg; His mother laments for his father.

**Celebrate **means acknowledge (a significant or happy day or event) with a social gathering or enjoyable activity.

For eg; They were celebrating their victory.

**Appeal **means to make a serious, urgent, or heartfelt request.

For eg; They were trying to make an appeal for the accident.

**Bemoan** means express discontent or sorrow over (something).

For eg; They were no use bemoaning the incident.
